newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market quiet, Iraq talk supportive.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market quiet, Iraq talk supportive.

text.p: Vietnam's rice market has remained very quiet in the past week, with buyers looking to supplies from Thailand and Pakistan for better value, traders said on Thursday.
However, local prices have firmed due to demand from the north of the country, where supplies have been badly affected this year by flooding and storms.
Export prices have been underpinned by rumours that Vietnam may be awarded a tender from Iraq for up to 60,000 tonnes of January/February delivery rice.
"There are a lot of rumours going around at the moment, including the Iraq one," said one trader in Ho Chi Minh City. "That, combined with thinner stocks, has been supportive."
Five percent broken grade was quoted at around $280-285 per tonne FOB Saigon Port, up around $5 from a week ago, while 10 percent was quoted about $5-10 higher at $275 per tonne.
Iraq is expected to issue a series of tenders to buy commodities over a six-month period when it will be selling oil in exchange for food under a $2 billion deal approved by the United Nations.

Dealers said talk that Iraq could take Vietnamese rice had swirled since a newspaper report earlier this month quoting Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh as saying the two countries could exchange for oil once the U.N. embargo was eased.
The report said that, even in the absence of such an agreement, Vietnam would continue to export rice to Iraq as repayment in kind for debt over the next four years.

The debt, the size of which has not been disclosed, stems from aid given by Baghdad during the Vietnam War. Hanoi has been repaying the debt in kind for years by sending tens of thousands of tonnes of rice annually and also Vietnamese workers to Iraq.
Traders in Vietnam gave a cautious welcome to Mexico's move to reopen its market and lift a blanket 1994 import ban that had blocked all foreign rice, but exempted shipments from the United States.
"It is good news for Asia in general," said one trader. "But I can't see Mexico suddenly knocking on Vietnam's door for a lot of rice. There are bound to be worries still about quality."

Dealers said there had been six shipments from Saigon Port in the past week, of which one was bound for Cuba. One dealer said there were four or five currently loading, all of them for government-to-government sales rather than commercial sales.
